5613.loc: p. 53, section 1.1.3.2 Systeme tonal mbuun; TBU sentence p. 49, section 1.1.3
5613.idn: Name in the source: mbuun (B87); Mbuun (Mbunda); parlers d'Imbongo; parler d'Idiofa

tn.quote: La langue mbuun a recours à deux tons simples H et B. Les réalisations contextuelles de ces deux tons en modulation conduisent à des tons montants et descendants. Ces tons modulés résultent des contacts entre deux tons simples. Le ton descendant est plus fréquent que le ton montant. Toutefois, malgré le défaut de paires minimales opposant le ton descendant au ton montant, nous pensons que le mbuun a quatre registres tonals: H, B et HB (descendant) et BH (montant).
tn.translation: The Mbuun language uses two simple tones, H and L. The contextual realisations of these two tones in modulation lead to rising and falling tones. These modulated tones result from contacts between two simple tones. The falling tone is more frequent than the rising tone. However, despite the lack of minimal pairs opposing the falling tone to the rising tone, we think that Mbuun has four tonal registers: H, L and HL (falling) and LH (rising).
tn.cite: Koni Muluwa, Joseph. 2010. Plantes, animaux et champignons en langues bantu: étude comparée de phytonymes, zoonymes et myconymes en nsong, ngong, mpiin, mbuun et hungan (Bandundu, RD Congo). Thèse de doctorat, Université Libre de Bruxelles, Faculté de Philosophie et Lettres (promoteurs K. Bostoen et A. Shango Mutambwe; soutenue le 28 juin 2010), 559 pp.
tn.locator: p. 53, section 1.1.3.2 Systeme tonal mbuun; TBU sentence p. 49, section 1.1.3
tn.note: Two level tones H/L; falling and rising treated as H+L / L+H on one syllable nucleus but listed as four 'registres tonals'; tonal minimal pairs given (oka 'poil' vs 'serpent'); nothing on stress. Checked against the source (tone consistency check round 3, 2026-09-24): system level-or-register -> level-and-contour (p. 53, section 1.1.3.2 Système tonal mbuun).

corr.words: Ces tons modulés résultent des contacts entre deux tons simples. ... nous pensons que le mbuun a quatre registres tonals: H, B et HB (descendant) et BH (montant). ... Néanmoins, dans la mesure où il existe des noms avec ce ton montant, même s'ils sont rarissimes ou ne s'opposent à rien d'autre, nous considérons ce registre.

5614.idn: Name in the source: Nafaara (Gur, Senufo subgroup; dialects Pantera and Fantera; studied at Banda-Ahenkro)

tn.quote: ²Nafaara has the following consonant phonemes: stops p b t d č j k g kp gb, fricatives f v s z š h, laterals l r, nasals m n ny ŋ, and semivowels w y. The vowels are i e ɛ a u o ɔ. All may be lengthened, symbolized by writing them double … There are three tones: high, mid, and low. See Carol Jordan's study of Nafaara phonology for more details. … [p. 86] The fusion of pé 'they' with wè 'future' results in a tone glide. Continuative nà works in the same manner, but is distinct in tone from ná 'past'.
tn.cite: Jordan, Dean L. 1978. Nafaara tense-aspect in the folk tale. In Joseph E. Grimes (ed.), Papers on discourse, 84-90. Summer Institute of Linguistics Publications in Linguistics and Related Fields 51. Dallas: Summer Institute of Linguistics.
tn.note: Three level tones (high, mid, low) stated in a phonology footnote; examples marked with acute, grave and some macrons; fused pronoun+particle forms carry a tone glide. Nothing on downstep or stress.

refs.ref: Stirtz, Timothy M. 2011. Laarim (loh) Tone. SIL Electronic Working Papers 2011-012, November 2011. Dallas: SIL International. 91 pp.

5615.loc: p. 4, section 0 Introduction (paragraphs 2 and 4); restated in Abstract p. 1 and 1.2.1 p. 16

tn.quote: Laarim has High and Low level tone and the tone-bearing unit is the syllable. Contour tone is rare and analyzed as two level tones on the same syllable. In noun roots, there are five contrastive tone melodies in the same syllable pattern: H, L, Lh (Low, floating High), HL, and LH. In verb roots, there are only three contrastive melodies H, L, Lh1. … Laarim also has automatic down-step, where Low tone following High tone is lower than a previous Low, and High tone following Low tone is lower than a previous High.
tn.cite: Stirtz, Timothy M. 2011. Laarim (loh) Tone. SIL Electronic Working Papers 2011-012, November 2011. Dallas: SIL International. 91 pp.
tn.locator: p. 4, section 0 Introduction (paragraphs 2 and 4); restated in Abstract p. 1 and 1.2.1 p. 16
tn.note: Two level tones, High and Low; syllable is the TBU, rare contours are level sequences; 5 noun-root and 3 verb-root melodies; floating H, automatic downstep, much grammatical tone; nothing on stress. Checked against the source (tone consistency check, 2026-09-23): p. 18 (frames paragraph); cf. p. 21 'Automatic downstep …).

tn.quote: These disyllabic nouns fall into three tonal classes and these tonal classes cut across the noun class system … In citation form, tone class I has a low-tone prefix followed by a low-tone stem … Before pause the low-tone stem is realised as a low fall. tn.quote: Underlyingly, only the high and low tones exist in this language. What we observe on the surface (downstepped or upstepped high tones and upstepped low tones) is due to different phonological and/or tonological processes that are operational in the language. ... Contour tones also exist in Njém but are treated as sequences of level tones. ... the tone-bearing unit in this language is the syllable because both light mono-moraic and heavy bi-moraic syllables can bear a similar number of tones.

refs.ref: 汪大年 [Wang Danian]. 1986. 妙齐提碑文研究(一)——十二世纪初缅甸语音初探 [A study of the Myazedi inscription (1): a first look at early-12th-century Burmese phonology]. 北京大学学报(哲学社会科学版) 1986(4): 103-118.

5619.loc: p. 116, section 三 声调 + p. 117, section 四 结语
5619.idn: Name in the source: 古缅语; “妙齐提”碑文时期缅语; 十二世纪初缅甸语

tn.quote: 在“妙齐提”碑文时期，只有元音长短之分还没有高平调出现，如果说，元音长短区别音位，可把它们算作声调。那么当时只有两个声调，一个短调，一个长调。妙碑中反映出来在古缅语中，有着较丰富的声母系统和辅音韵尾系统，因而声调的区别作用幷不突出，字音的高低变化，只是一种伴随特征。幷不具备音位功能。[p.117] 关于声调，我们的结论是：古缅语中只有长、短两调。后来的四个声调是历史发展的结果。[a']尾、[h]尾是分别表示短调和长调的一种符号。
tn.translation: In the period of the Myazedi inscription there was only a distinction of vowel length; no high-level tone had yet appeared. If one takes vowel length as phonemically distinctive, one may count them as tones; then there were only two tones at the time, a short tone and a long tone. As the inscription shows, Old Burmese had a fairly rich system of initials and consonant codas, so the distinguishing role of tone was not prominent; variation in the pitch of syllables was only a concomitant feature and had no phonemic function. ... On tone, our conclusion is: Old Burmese had only two 'tones', long and short. The later four tones are the result of historical development. …
tn.cite: 汪大年 [Wang Danian]. 1986. 妙齐提碑文研究(一)——十二世纪初缅甸语音初探 [A study of the Myazedi inscription (1): a first look at early-12th-century Burmese phonology]. 北京大学学报(哲学社会科学版) 1986(4): 103-118.
tn.locator: p. 116, section 三 声调 + p. 117, section 四 结语
tn.note: Author posits only a long vs short vowel-length '调' contrast, pitch explicitly non-phonemic; coded as no tone. One could instead record 2 length 'tones' (短调, 长调). Argued from inscription spellings. Quotation re-keyed from the printed page on 2026-09-24.

5622.idn: Name in the source: KiYaka (also YiYaka, IYaka, Yaka, Kiyaka; Bantu H31), dialect of Mulopo-Ndiindi

tn.quote: As was mentioned earlier, KiYaka has three phonetic tones: L, H, and R. To account for the different surface tonal phenomena, I propose that KiYaka has basically the H-L opposition supplemented by accent. The H is specified underlyingly and can be prelinked or floating, but the L is supplied by default according to the following rule: … As for the R, I suggest that it is just the phonetic realisation of H on accented syllables. Specifically, the H is converted into R by the following phonetic rule. (13) H-RAISING: Realise an accented syllable linked to H as R.
tn.cite: Kidima, Lukowa. 1991. Tone and Accent in KiYaka. PhD dissertation, University of California, Los Angeles (committee chair Bruce Hayes), xiv+238 pp. [thesis by the author of the cited, unconfirmed Lincom title: Kidima, Lukowa. 199-. Tone and phonological phrasing in KiYaka. Munchen: Lincom Europa]
tn.locator: pp. 22-23, section 2.3.2 Accent; see also 2.1 Phonetic Tones p. 13 and 2.3.4.3 Rule Inventory pp. 47-48.
tn.note: Two-way tone contrast, H vs default L, plus a lexical accent (stem-initial, partly contrastive by mora) that raises a docked H to extra-high R; floating H tones donated rightward in the clitic group.
